discussion_comments.comment_body: This is not equivalent to `127.0.0.1` - using `localhost` may result in `::1` being used instead since `localhost` has both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses

We need to ensure that the order here is retained, since IE8 breaks if `filename*` is first in the header. Since we're unpacking the dict, we can't ensure order. One solution is to patch Werkzeug to allow `*args` to `headers.add`, then pass tuples `('filename, ...), ('filename*', ...)`.
If we don't care about supporting IE8, we can ignore this. @untitaker @ThiefMaster thoughts?

For reference, DISA (US mil) [requires](http://iase.disa.mil/stigs/app-security/browser-guidance/Pages/index.aspx) IE10 or 11 to be certified, so even big gov deployments can't be on a network without that. I feel fairly confident in not supporting IE8.

Changing the Headers API to care about ordering of options would require a refactor. I don't think that is warranted for a workaround for older browsers.

We could check if the filename fits into ASCII and omit `filename*` accordingly. Then the user can decide whether they want to support IE8 or not.
Just realized that even if we enhance `Headers.add`, we still can't use it because we can't guarantee that projects are using the latest Werkzeug version. 😞
